headline: Ryan Blaney’s 94-Point Gap Was Pure Bad Luck

paragraphs.text: Ryan Blaney had a career year in 2026 and still lost the crown by a razor-thin margin. With a gap of just 94 points, he was once again on the verge of securing a NASCAR Cup Series championship. He finished fourth in the standings, just behind champion Kyle Larson. This tiny gap came after Blaney earned his fourth win of the season, tying a career-high mark. He also secured his 21st career win overall. Per Yahoo Sports, this was his third top-five points finish in the last five seasons.

Blaney set new personal bests for laps led with 1,107 and top-10 finishes with 23. He also claimed five poles, the most in his career. His average finish of 12.7 was his best in a NextGen Cup season. Yet, four bad races in the final stretch undid all that hard work. In the final 10 races, four results of 33rd place or lower cost Blaney the title. Each of those disasters happened when he had a real shot at a top-10 spot.
The Three Races That Cost a Title

Three specific crashes at three different tracks wiped out his title hopes. Although Blaney placed fourth in every stage at Gateway, his final position was 35th. A blown brake rotor caused the issue, a problem NASCAR fixed the very next week. That single bad finish cost him at least 31 points he would have likely gained. Then came Bristol, where Blaney was running second before Carson Hocevar put him into the wall. Even a third-place finish there would have given him another 31 points. Hocevar later fought with Blaney on pit road, but the damage to the points was already done.

The final blow happened at Martinsville. Josh Berry brake-checked Blaney, ruining his chances for an eighth-place stage finish and ending his race. Berry went on to finish fourth. If Blaney had posted a comparable result, he would have lost those stage points, and the margin needed to beat Larson would have risen above 94 points. These three incidents alone cost him well over 100 points. The new format demands consistency every single week, and Blaney simply could not get it in the final 10 races.
2027 Looks Different With a New Car

Blaney does not need to hang his head over this loss. He had a career-high season that proved he can win four races in a row. The Ford team is already looking ahead with a new body design. The new Ford body offers superior turning capability in traffic and enhanced overall performance. Blaney will be the face of that new car in 2027. He might be the next driver pictured next to the Bill France Cup. The 94-point gap was a matter of bad luck, not a lack of speed.
